selected_evidence.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance
selected_evidence.summary: The policy applied successfully; before and after reboot, `all`, `default`, `enp1s0`, and `lo` reported both controls as zero. The persistent root-owned configuration remained present after reboot.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered state. After reboot, the system was running with zero failed units, active NetworkManager and systemd-sysctl, restored addressing/routes, and preserved hardening values.

commands.command:
umask 022; install -o root -g root -m 0644 /dev/null /etc/sysctl.d/99-kernel-network-hardening.conf; cat > /etc/sysctl.d/99-kernel-network-hardening.conf <<'ANTRIEB_SYSCTL_EOF'
# Disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects and source-routed packets.
# "all" controls the aggregate policy, "default" covers future interfaces,
# and the wildcard applies the policy to interfaces already present.
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.*.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.*.accept_source_route = 0
ANTRIEB_SYSCTL_EOF
restorecon /etc/sysctl.d/99-kernel-network-hardening.conf 2>/dev/null || true
